title: Dwarves delving for gold and glory! A review and overview of Stalagbite!
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2CnmP8lvGE4

Daniel (@dungeondive) is smitten with Stalagbite!, a dwarven cavern-delving game from Midlam Miniatures reviewed from a feature-complete pre-production copy. One to six dwarves flip rock and cave tokens across double-sided cavern tiles hunting gold, gems and glory, fighting animated stalagmites, creeping jeepers and red hook horrors with custom d6 that can trigger counterattacks and crushing critical hits. A Goblin Hunting Party deck ticks down each time the event die shows an hourglass; when it empties, genuinely nasty goblins pour in through the marked entrance and everyone runs for the exit, spending glory to linger. Glory doubles as votes to trigger the endgame early, and one dead dwarf ends everything. Relics, single-use skills, an incident deck of falling rocks and awakening stalagmites, critical-hit and poison decks, and per-game cavern rule cards pile on variety, and a surprise lava cavern mini-expansion ships free in every copy. A six-game campaign carries relics and skills forward, with a finale scenario if nobody dies. Daniel wants more information cards (the goblins have none) and a way to gain skills mid-game, and admits the solo mode loses the voting and backstabbing that will make it shine with a group. He files it beside Dungeon Quest and marvels that a game like this arrived in 2024.

----

Stalagbite uses glory as score, as votes to flee and as a price for lingering. What is your favourite example of one resource pulling triple duty in a game?
